newsitem.title: THAILAND: Shan group says Burma forces mass relocations.
newsitem.headline: Shan group says Burma forces mass relocations.

text.p: Burma's military junta has forced more than 25,000 ethnic Shans from their homes and many who fear the government want to flee to Thailand, a Shan group said on Monday.

Loong Sa Wa Na, a Shan who fled to Thailand from the Laikha township after being relocated, said Burmese troops had relocated about 25,300 people from nearly 167 Shan villages since April, the Shan Youth Network Group (SYNG) said in a statement.
The statement quoted Loong Sa Wa Na as saying the Burmese troops had given the villagers five days to move or their houses would be burned down in this latest relocation.
"When the villagers were forced to relocate, SLORC did not take any responsibilities at the relocation site," the statement said, referring to the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council.

It said the relocation was not only disruptive to the villagers but also caused them economic hardship as most were farmers and the moves took place in the middle of the planting season. In addition, they were moved into over-populated areas of non-arable land, the statement said.
"These people are uncertain of their living," the statement said. "Because of many difficulties at the relocation site, most of the villagers want to come to Thailand for a safer living here."
Rebels are fighting for autonomy for central Shan state.
The relocations and reports of some killing of other villagers were part of a "four-cut" operation against the rebels, Shan guerrillas said.
The SLORC's "four-cut" operation is an effort to cut off information, supplies, intelligence and recruits from the rebels.
Earlier this month Shan and Thai army sources said the SLORC had massacred at least 58 civilians in June and commited other human rights abuses.
The Burmese government has denied the accusations.
A senior government official told Reuters by telephone from Rangoon that the reports of relocations and killings were just propaganda efforts by the Shan.
"There are no major military operations in those areas," said the official, who said the relocations and killings might be committed by splinter groups of the Shan.
